title: TarGATE: Target-Aware Data Selection via Token-Attenuation Gates
claim: Existing selection methods pick data skewed toward a few categories, while ours concentrates on the target capability via a simple gating module.
layout: 2 panels, left stacked bar chart, right architecture diagram, vertical flow upward
description: Two-panel figure. Panel (a), 'Data distribution', is a horizontal stacked bar chart comparing the share of data selected per category by TarGATE and baselines (Full Data, ToV, LESS, Grad-Sim, RDS+, Rep-Sim, BM25). Categories are Math Reasoning (green), Instruction Execution (blue), Code Engineering (purple), Dialogue Creative (teal), Structured Extraction (gold) and Safety Alignment (red). The TarGATE bar is almost entirely green at 99.7, while the baselines mirror the mixed full-data distribution or skew toward one category; ToV is 75.5 blue. Panel (b), 'Architecture of TarGATE', is a small vertical diagram. The input h_l^attn flows up into a Feed-Forward Network. Its output is multiplied by a gate made of Linear Projection, then Sigmoid, then a 0-1 slider. The product goes into an Add block through a residual connection. The orange gate box and the label 'Attenuate output of FFN' mark the key module.

abstract: Targeted instruction tuning requires selecting pertinent samples from massive mixed candidate datasets guided by a small reference dataset reflecting the desired capability, yet efficiently identifying high-quality data amidst noise remains challenging. To address this, we propose TarGATE ( Tar get-aware GATE s, a simple yet effective data selection framework that leverages the model's inherent data understanding. TarGATE computes a token-level Information Retention Ratio ( IRR ) to scale the output of the feed-forward network, where the instance-level average IRR serves as a quantitative metric for data quality. To align gates' preferences with the target task, we employ a joint optimization strategy utilizing the reference set and a subset of candidate data, which encourages the gates to assign higher IRRs to reference-aligned data while suppressing low-quality samples. Extensive experiments across noisy and real-world scenarios demonstrate that TarGATE outperforms related baselines. Furthermore, TarGATE exhibits superior computational efficiency and strong cross-model transferability, enabling smaller selector to effectively curate high-quality fine-tuning data for larger foundation models.
